extracted.intended_audience: readers, researchers, journalists, and organizations seeking MBFC's methodology for rating media bias, factuality, pollsters, and country/government assessments
extracted.subtask_description: Detailed methodology for systematically assessing news sources' ideological bias and factual reliability, plus procedures for rating pollsters, politicians, countries, and credibility. Describes sampling, scoring categories, weights, numeric scales, and procedural safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sampling requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: To ensure a thorough and accurate evaluation, our methodology requires reviewing a minimum of 10 headlines and 5 full news stories from each source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This allows analysis of language, framing, and tone in headlines and deeper examination of article content, sourcing, and presentation of facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: Analysts use manual searches for reporting patterns, keyword analyses, and comparisons with independent, verified sources to identify political affiliation, ideological leanings, and adherence to journalistic standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special attention is given to bias by omission, one-sided narratives, and use of unreliable sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human reviewers & AI use limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Human reviewers conduct all evaluations and scoring. Any use of AI tools (e.g., Grammarly) is strictly limited to grammar and text editing and does not influence scoring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MBFC (added 01/01/2026) requires that humans, not automated systems, be ultimately responsible for editorial decisions, accuracy, and accountability. Use of AI without meaningful human editorial oversight may lead to a Questionable rating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bias Scoring System — categories & weights
rubrics_metrics.description: Placement on the Left-Right Bias Scale is determined by a weighted composite score derived from four categories: Economic System (35%), Social Progressive Liberalism vs. Traditional Social Conservatism (35%), Straight News Reporting Balance (15%), and Editorial Bias (15%). Scores are on a scale of -10 to +10; the weighted average determines the overall bias score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each category is assigned a numerical value from -10 to +10 (directional), multiplied by its weight, and summed to produce an overall bias score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic System (35%)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluates the economic ideology the source promotes, from communism to no-regulation capitalism (scale -10 to +10).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numeric anchors provided: -10 Communism; -7.5 Socialism; -5 Democratic Socialism; -2.5 Regulated Market Economy; 0 Centrism; +2.5 Moderately Regulated Capitalism; +5 Classical Liberalism; +7.5 Libertarianism; +10 Radical Laissez-Faire Capitalism. Consider content that promotes regulation levels, corporatism, and public vs private ownership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social Progressive Liberalism vs. Traditional Social Conservatism (35%)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures the source's stance on social values and advocacy (e.g., Abortion, Immigration, Climate Change, Social Justice, Equity), on a -10 to +10 scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numeric anchors: -10 Strong Progressive Liberalism; -7.5 Progressive Liberalism; -5 Moderate Progressive Liberalism; -2.5 Mild Progressive Liberalism; 0 Balanced; +2.5 Mild Conservatism; +5 Moderate Conservatism; +7.5 Traditional Conservatism; +10 Strong Traditional Conservatism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Straight News Reporting Balance (15%)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures how well a source reports all sides in its straight news stories, either through story selection or content balance within articles (scale -10 to +10).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anchors: -10 Extreme Left Reporting; -7.5 Strong Left Reporting; -5 Moderate Left Reporting; -2.5 Mild Left Reporting; 0 Neutral/Balanced; +2.5 Mild Right Reporting; +5 Moderate Right Reporting; +7.5 Strong Right Reporting; +10 Extreme Right Reporting. This category is distinct from editorials/op-eds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial Bias (15%)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluates bias expressed through opinion pieces, editorials, and the use of loaded emotional language favoring one side (scale -10 to +10).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anchors mirror reporting scale with descriptors from Extreme Left Editorial Bias (-10) to Extreme Right Editorial Bias (+10). Look for emotionally charged or manipulative language in opinion content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bias Scoring Levels (range mapping)
rubrics_metrics.description: Numeric overall bias score ranges map to categorical labels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mapping: -10 to -8.0 = Extreme Left Bias; -7.9 to -5.0 = Left Bias (Far Left at -7.0+); -4.9 to -2.0 = Left-Center Bias; -1.9 to +1.9 = Least Biased; +2.0 to +4.9 = Right-Center Bias; +5.0 to +7.9 = Right Bias (Far Right at +7.0+); +8.0 to +10 = Extreme Right Bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factual Reporting Scoring System — categories & weights
rubrics_metrics.description: Factual reporting score is derived from four weighted categories: Failed Fact Checks (40%), Sourcing (25%), Transparency (25%), and One-Sidedness/Omission (10%). Each category is scored 0–10; the weighted average determines factuality rating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each component has explicit scoring criteria and explanations; scores are combined via weighted average to determine factual rating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failed Fact Checks (40%)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fact-check records from credible third-party organizations over the past five years are analyzed. Only uncorrected errors negatively impact the score. Instances of undocumented misinformation, conspiracy promotion, and pseudoscience are considered. Scored 0–10, where 0 = no failed fact checks and 10 = ten or more failed fact checks or confirmed cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scale: 0 none; 1 one failed; 2 two failed; ...; 10 ten or more. Promotion of pseudoscience or conspiracies typically results in scores ≥5. Corrected fact checks do not negatively impact the score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sourcing (25%)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures credibility and depth of references, including proper citations and hyperlinks to external, credible sources (scored 0–10).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 0 = Perfect sourcing; 1 = Almost perfect; ...; 5 = Mixed sourcing (credible and questionable); ...; 10 = No sourcing or complete reliance on discredited sources. Sources without hyperlinks/explicit citations automatically score 5 or higher.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency (25%)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assesses disclosure of ownership, funding, authorship, mission, and location (scored 0–10).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 0 = Fully transparent (all five elements clearly disclosed); 1 near full; ...; 5 partially transparent (two of five disclosed); ...; 10 = No transparency at all. Explanation emphasizes importance of About page, ownership identification, major donors, and at least country/state/city and person responsible.

rubrics_metrics.name: One-Sidedness / Bias Omission / Propaganda (10%)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluates extent to which a source provides balanced perspectives vs exhibiting ideological bias or propaganda, including use of emotional/loaded language (scored 0–10).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scale: 0 Perfect balance; 1 Almost balanced; 2 Minor bias; ...; 5 Noticeable bias; ...; 10 Extreme bias or propaganda. Explanation notes that scale reflects ideological balance and degree of rhetorical/emotional manipulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factuality Rating Levels (numeric mapping)
rubrics_metrics.description: Numeric factual weighted score maps to categorical factuality ratings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mapping: 0 = Very High; 0.1–1.9 = High; 2.0–4.4 = Mostly Factual; 4.5–6.4 = Mixed; 6.5–8.4 = Low; 8.5–10 = Very Low. (Separate simplified IFCN-derived factual scale also appears in alternate section.)

rubrics_metrics.name: MBFC Credibility Rating (10-point system)
rubrics_metrics.description: Credibility is assessed on a 10-point scale prioritizing Factual Reporting, then Bias, then Traffic/Longevity, with an age bonus and press freedom penalties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Components: Factual Reporting points (Very High=4, High=3, Mostly Factual=2, Mixed=1, Low=0); Bias points (Least Biased/Pro-Science=3, Right-/Left-Center=2, Left or Right=1, Questionable/Conspiracy/Pseudoscience=0); Traffic/Longevity (High=2, Medium=1, Minimal=0); Bonus +1 for existence ≥10 years; Press Freedom: Limited Freedom = -1, Total Oppression = -2. Credibility classification: High = 6+, Medium = 3–5 (or Mostly Factual 3.6–4.5 automatically = Medium), Low = 0–2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Politician Ratings — bias scoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Bias placement for politicians is determined by evaluating two primary dimensions: Economic System and Social Progressive vs Traditional Conservatism, each weighted at 50%; composite determines Left–Right placement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Economic System scale anchors (-10 Communism to +10 Radical Laissez-Faire); Social Values scale anchors (-10 Strong Progressive to +10 Strong Traditional Conservatism). Composite score mapped to same bias rating scale used for sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: New Pollster Rating Methodology (2026)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pollster bias rating prioritizes measurable polling performance: Polling Bias Assessment (70%) using Silver Bulletin's mean-reverted bias metric and Editorial Bias Assessment (30%) for published commentary. Polling bias is signed (left negative, right positive) and calibrated to discrete scores based on absolute mean-reverted bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calibration example: absolute 0.0–0.5 → 1, 0.6–1.0 → 2, 1.1–1.5 → 3, 1.6–2.0 → 4, etc. Final Bias Score = (Polling Bias Score × 0.70) + (Editorial Bias Score × 0.30). Classification: 0.0–1.9 Least Biased, 2.0–4.9 Left-/Right-Center, 5.0–7.9 Left/Right, 8.0+ Extreme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pollster Editorial Bias Assessment (30%)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluates ideological framing in commentary/analysis published by a polling organization on a 0–10 scale and assigns a directional value; used only when commentary exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designed to be secondary to polling performance; consistent ideological framing (not isolated articles) is measured.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pollster factual reporting mapping
rubrics_metrics.description: Pollster factual reporting is based on Silver Bulletin's pollster letter grades mapped to MBFC factual categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mapping: A+ → Very High Factual; A to A− → High Factual; B+ to B− → Mostly Factual; C+ to C− → Mixed Factual; D and below → Low Factual. Credibility still assessed separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Old Pollster Rating Methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Earlier approach derived bias from FiveThirtyEight's mean-reverted bias and factual reporting from FiveThirtyEight's overall star ratings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bias categorization: 0 to +0.9 Least Biased; 1.0–2.4 Left/Right-Center; 2.5+ Left/Right. Factual reporting mapped via 538 star metric to Very High/High/Mostly/Mixed/Low factual categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Country Freedom Rating
rubrics_metrics.description: A country's level of freedom is assessed by averaging Reporters Without Borders (RSF) and Freedom House's Freedom in the World Index (both 0–100).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combined score ranges: 100–90 Excellent Freedom; 89–70 Mostly Free; 69–50 Moderate Freedom; 49–25 Limited Freedom; 24–0 Total Oppression. If either index is unavailable, alternative credible sources (UNESCO, Statista, BBC Country Profiles) are used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Country Government Bias Rating
rubrics_metrics.description: Country government bias is determined by examining the head of state and their party positions plus the country's economic system; right-left designation is mainly determined by economic policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Economic system (capitalism, socialism, etc.) carries more weight than social agenda when assigning right-left designation; country profiles include bias arrows like source pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fact-Check Verification — use of IFCN-affiliated fact-checkers
rubrics_metrics.description: MBFC incorporates findings from fact-checkers affiliated with the International Fact-Checking Network (IFCN); only fact checks from the last five years are considered and corrected fact checks do not negatively impact a rating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Credible third-party fact-check records are used in the Failed Fact Checks category; MBFC rarely conducts original fact checks and primarily relies on IFCN-affiliated organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and Accountability criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Transparency assessment focuses on disclosure of funding, organizational structure, methodology, ownership, mission, authorship, and location.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lack of an About page or failure to disclose ownership/major donors/authors reduces credibility. Inadequate transparency typically results in reducing the source's factual reporting rating by one or two levels depending on severity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Questionable Sources classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Questionable sources display extreme bias, propaganda, unreliable sourcing, or lack transparency; they may disseminate fake news for profit or influence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A source lacking transparency in mission, ownership, or authorship is automatically categorized as Questionable. Sources from countries with significant government censorship may also be deemed Questionable; such sources require article-by-article fact-checking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conspiracy / Pseudoscience classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Sources that disseminate unverified conspiracy theories or pseudoscientific claims (e.g., climate denial, anti-vaccination) are placed in this category when such content is a primary focus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referencing the Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy on Science and Pseudoscience, MBFC requires the source's primary focus to involve conspiracies/pseudoscience for this classification. See MBFC's Pseudoscience Dictionary for examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI-Generated Content and Editorial Oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of AI in content creation is allowed for editing/grammar/formatting, but publishing AI-generated articles without human oversight harms credibility. AI-generated images are not inherently disqualifying but may reduce ratings if misleading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable uses: grammar/spelling correction, editing for clarity, summarizing human-written text, assisting research organization. Unacceptable uses: publishing AI-generated articles with no human review, failing to identify responsible editor/author, mass-producing content lacking sourcing/originality. AI imagery that is deceptive or used for propaganda can contribute to Questionable rating or lower factual reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Traffic Estimates thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Traffic is estimated using SimilarWeb and other metrics; categories determine Traffic/Longevity points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minimal Traffic: under 250K page views/print/media market viewers per month; Medium Traffic: 250K to 3M per month; High Traffic: over 3M per month. For print/TV, subscribers and market size are considered. If data unavailable, best estimates are used.

rubrics_metrics.name: IFCN Fact-Checking Principles adherence
rubrics_metrics.description: MBFC News adheres to the International Fact-Checking Network Fact-checkers' Code of Principles (Poynter Institute): nonpartisanship/fairness, transparency of sources, transparency of funding & organization, transparency of methodology, and open/ honest corrections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MBFC follows these principles for all fact checks: apply same standards to all sides; provide sources for replication (except where safety is a concern); disclose funding and organizational details; explain methodology; publish and follow corrections policy.
